newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Captive Colombia troops arrive for handover.
newsitem.headline: Captive Colombia troops arrive for handover.

text.p: Scores of soliders taken prisoner on Aug. 30 of last year began arriving in this remote jungle town on Sunday for their release at a ceremony orchestrated by Marxist-led Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels.

The rebels' handover of the 60 soldiers, and of 10 marines captured in a firefight in northwest Choco province in January, marks the end of Latin America's longest-running hostage crisis -- a drama that was largely overshadowed by the recent siege of the Japanese embassy residence in Lima.

"I'm in good health, everything is fine, they treated us well," said the first soldier to climb down off a Russian-made Mi-17 helicopter loaned to the International Committee of the Red Cross by Colombia's army to transport the captive troops from an undisclosed jungle location.
The solider, who did not give his name, said he wanted to stay in the army despite his ordeal.
Two hours before the helicopter arrived, a column of FARC troops secured the town's main square to make way for the official handover ceremony due at 10 a.m. (1500 GMT).

The Aug. 30 raid on a jungle army base, in which 60 troops were captured and at least 27 others were killed, marked one of the FARC's biggest military victories in recent years. Robert Pastor of the Carter Foundation in the United States, on hand for the soldiers' release here, said he viewed it as "important because it could be the chance to end Latin America's longest- running guerrilla war."
